metadata.source: v9 R pipeline outputs, chapter 6 of the underlying thesis

sensitivity_4d_vs_5d.description: Removing the five subjective wellbeing variables (CASP-12, loneliness, hope_future, interest, expect_alive) from the clustering input. The 4D solution is fitted on the same pipeline, k held fixed at 5 (Italy) and 6 (Sweden). Life satisfaction is external to both specifications and serves as impartial validator.
sensitivity_4d_vs_5d.interpretation: The 4D solution is marginally tighter on internal metrics (clustering on fewer variables produces tighter partitions in a reduced space) but loses substantial external discriminative power on life satisfaction: -41% in Italy, -22% in Sweden. The adjusted Rand index between 4D and 5D partitions is 0.41 (Italy) and 0.52 (Sweden), meaning roughly half of the assignments differ. The 5D specification preserves a substantively important contrast (Fragile Resigned vs Fragile Depressed) that the 4D solution collapses.

kmeans_lca_convergence.description: Profile-level convergence rate between K-means hard assignment and the modal LCA class. LCA fitted with poLCA (Linzer & Lewis 2011) on tertilised inputs, k = 5/6 to match K-means. Profiles ordered by convergence descending within each country.
kmeans_lca_convergence.interpretation: Profiles at the extremes of the distribution are most robust: Fragile Resigned (Italy) converges at 95.6%, Connected Wealthy (Sweden) at 86.9%, Fragile (Sweden) at 85.9%. Middle-range profiles converge at 54-66%, indicating substantive latent types with soft boundaries. The Swedish welfare-regime-specific profiles (Wealthy Digital, Asset Rich) converge below 55%, consistent with their interpretive role as composite signatures rather than crystallised types.

multi_algorithm.description: K-means compared against three agglomerative alternatives across k = 2 to 12 on six internal validity indexes. Reported for the chosen k (5 for Italy, 6 for Sweden).
multi_algorithm.summary: Across both countries and across all six indexes (R^2, Pseudo-F, silhouette, Davies-Bouldin proxy, Dunn, Pearson-gamma), K-means attains uniformly higher within-cluster R^2 and silhouette than Ward, complete linkage, and average linkage. Ward linkage is competitive only on the Dunn index, which penalises cluster elongation differently and is known to favour ellipsoidal shapes.

duda_hart.comment: Pseudo-T^2 (Duda-Hart) for Ward linkage peaks at k = 5 (Italy) and k = 6 (Sweden), independently corroborating the K-means cut-off. Average and complete linkages produce shallower peaks consistent with their known behaviour on mixed-scale data.

factor_analysis_stability.heywood_case: Sweden social_integration loading 1.11, communality 1.38. Flagged as a known fragility of the Swedish factor solution; the decision to cluster on standardised original variables rather than on factor scores insulates the segmentation from this instability.
